structure: Part 1 of 3 read ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm.md lines 1-374 in full: the verbatim quote of Sam's answers (lines 1-110, with points 1, 3, 3a, 3b and 6 claimed here; points 2, 4, 5, 7, 7a, 7b, 8, 8a and 9 are read only as context for later parts), the preamble at lines 111-136 (orchestrator-versus-Sam marking, what ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers instead, the four evidence files, the design-question numbering), and sections (a) to (d) at lines 137-374: (a) search boxes, listed claims 1-4; (b) the JavaScript rule, 5-7; (c) ask-design rows and design questions 1-13, 8-22; (d) rows built with GOV.UK or MoJ or kept as today, 23-27. Claims follow the file's order: preamble first, then Sam's quoted decisions, then each listed claim split into one fact per claim. Listed claims marked 'Sam (point N)' are verbatim where the quote says them in so many words; claims marked as the orchestrator's application are recorded as inferred, with the quote taken from the ruling file's listed claim and the note naming the principle. Gaps record what the quote and claims leave open (the dropdown's content in point 1, Sam's hedged wording in 3a, the pop-up lean in point 6, and the outstanding design answers).

claims.statement: A listed claim that says 'applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle (point N)' is the orchestrator's application of a principle, not Sam's own ruling; a claim that says 'Sam (point N)' is decided by Sam's quoted words.
claims.quote: Where a claim is the orchestrator's application of a principle and not Sam's own ruling, it says "applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle (point N)". Where it says "Sam (point N)", his words above make the decision.
claims.note: Applies to every listed claim in this ruling; the reconciler should weigh orchestrator claims below Sam's own.

claims.statement: Sam does not want lists of row ids brought back to him to confirm, so the orchestrator applies his principles to the backlog rows itself and records its calls in this ruling.
claims.quote: Sam said not to bring him lists of row ids to confirm. So the orchestrator has applied his principles to the rows itself, and its calls are recorded here
claims.note: Calls are taken from answers-2026-10-09-pm.md sections 3c, 7, 7a, 7c and 8.

claims.statement: Sam's reply to being brought row lists under point 3b rejects being asked to confirm rows one by one; this is inferred from the tone of his reply, which the preamble reads as 'do not bring row ids to confirm'.
claims.quote: Why come back to me with that shit?
claims.note: The quote itself does not say what to do instead; the preamble at line 111 is the main session's reading of it.

claims.statement: ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates, a separate ruling made the same day, covers narrowing the dashboard block to the summary information, the notification lists staying in each frontend, templates going ahead with template mode, and the plants calls for the templates theme; this ruling does not restate those claims and only refers to them.
claims.quote: ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates is a separate ruling made the same day. It covers:

claims.statement: The ruling's evidence is four files: search-component/findings-2026-10-09.md (where the accessible autocomplete is used, read from each repo's origin/main on 9 October), js-triage/triage-2026-10-09.md (per-row triage, library check and 12 design questions), overview-ownership/findings-2026-10-09.md (ownership of overview, review, declaration and confirmation) and plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json (per-row plants equivalents).
claims.quote: js-triage/triage-2026-10-09.md: the per-row triage, the library check and the 12 questions for design

claims.statement: Design question numbers in this ruling are the triage file's numbers, and question 13 is new in this ruling.
claims.quote: Design question numbers below are the triage file's numbers. Question 13 is new in this ruling.

claims.statement: Sam: the prototype's search controls are not accessible and do not use GDS components.
claims.quote: the prototype isn't accessible. It's not using some GDS stuff.
claims.note: answers point 1 of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md (search boxes).

claims.statement: Sam: for search boxes the precedence is not 'prototype always wins'; the component used may be the one already in the real frontends.
claims.quote: the sort of precedence needs to be a little bit different than prototype always wins. In terms of
claims.note: Continues: 'the component being used, it might be the one that's actually in the frontend or frontends.'

claims.statement: Sam's point 1 leaves open what a search dropdown such as the country list contains: he says it needs more input and that neither the frontend nor the prototype is simply right on it. Listed claim 2 settles the entries by citing claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 (MDM via reference-data), not by these words.
claims.note: Sam's words: 'The content of that dropdown, if it's a country dropdown, what's in it? That might still need a bit more input'.

claims.statement: Sam: the prototype's JavaScript behaviour is not GDS compliant and must not be copied into the frontend by adding a lot of JavaScript, for accessibility and maintainability reasons.
claims.quote: This isn't stuff that can just be blindly replicated by chucking a tonne of JavaScript in the frontend.

claims.statement: Sam: GOV.UK (GDS) components are the toolbox; where they have nothing, another tested, accessible government library such as the Ministry of Justice's or the Scottish Government's is used.
claims.quote: We really try to strictly head here to GDS components as a toolbox, and where that's not available, use other
claims.note: Continues: 'government libraries like a Ministry of Justice or a Scottish Government component that has been tested and meets accessibility requirements.'

claims.statement: Sam: graceful degradation is required, so every page must work without JavaScript, and CSS and JavaScript may only enhance it; the prototype's way of doing something may therefore not be possible or wanted in the real service.
claims.quote: It needs to be able to work without
claims.note: Full wording spans lines 25-28: 'We've got a graceful degradation requirement on this ... It needs to be able to work without JavaScript'.

claims.statement: Sam: as a pre-step for an affected increment, three questions are answered in order (is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other off-the-shelf complementary components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required), and then it goes back to design to argue it is not needed.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff:

claims.statement: Sam: each 'ask design' row needs its own check-in with design, and a purely JavaScript functionality change is questioned and blocked on design.
claims.quote: I think with the ask design rows, they need individual check-ins.

claims.statement: Sam: an 'ask design' row is built in its no-JavaScript version, with a second increment blocked waiting on design, and the design-blocked work goes in its own theme.
claims.quote: Almost both implement the no-JS version and have another increment which is blocked waiting on design, and the design block stuff

claims.statement: Sam's wording in point 3a is hedged ('I really don't know. Almost ...'), so the quote leaves open how firm the split into a no-JavaScript increment and a design-blocked increment is; listed claim 8 records it as his ruling without that hedge.
Sam: live filtering waits on design.
claims.quote: Yeah, that live filtering has to wait on design.

claims.statement: Sam: the amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete area needs JavaScript checks, and pop-ups feel non-GDS, so he leans towards not building them.
claims.quote: It feels very non-GDS to have popups, so I'm leaning towards we won't do this.
claims.note: The transcript's last sentence of point 6 is unclear and nothing rests on it (lines 71-72).

claims.statement: Sam: anything in the amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete area that is not about adding pop-ups may survive.
claims.quote: If there's anything in there that isn't around adding popups, then maybe that survives.
